messages.content:
You are given one person (a thinker), the lead section of their encyclopedia article (EXTRACT), and a list of historical events and periods whose dates overlap the person's life (EVENTS, each with an id).

Say which of the listed events bear on this person, and how. Use only the EXTRACT: if the extract does not mention or clearly imply an event, do not connect it, even if you know the connection from elsewhere. An event that merely happened during the person's life is not a connection unless the extract brings it up.

For each connection give:
- "event": the id from the EVENTS list, exactly as written (Q followed by digits). Never an event that is not in the list.
- "type", one of:
  - "lived_through": the extract mentions the event as part of the person's circumstances, without saying they acted in it or wrote against it;
  - "took_part_in": the person acted in the event (fought, sat in the assembly, negotiated, signed, governed, led);
  - "wrote_in_response_to": a named work, or the person's writing generally, answers or treats the event; put the work's title in "work" if the extract names one;
  - "suffered_under": the person was exiled, imprisoned, censored, dismissed, persecuted or killed because of the event;
  - "shaped_by": the extract says the event formed the person's thinking, without naming a work.
- "reason": one sentence in your own words.
- "evidence": one sentence copied exactly from the EXTRACT, character for character, that supports the connection. Do not paraphrase, shorten or join sentences.
- "work": the title of the work, if the type is wrote_in_response_to and the extract names it; otherwise an empty string.

If an event in the list is the same thing under a broader or narrower name as one the extract mentions (the extract says "the civil war" and the list has "English Civil War"), connect it. If nothing in the extract bears on any listed event, return an empty list. Return JSON only, matching the schema you are given.

PERSON: Thales (624 BCE–540s BCE). ancient Greek philosopher and mathematician

EXTRACT:
Thales of Miletus ( THAY-leez; Ancient Greek: Θαλῆς; c. 626/623  – c. 548/545 BC) was a pre-Socratic Greek philosopher from Miletus in Ionia, Asia Minor. Thales was one of the Seven Sages, founding figures of Ancient Greece.
Beginning in eighteenth-century historiography, many came to regard him as the first philosopher in the Greek tradition, breaking from the prior use of mythology to explain the world and instead using natural philosophy. He is thus otherwise referred to as the first to have engaged in mathematics, science, and deductive reasoning.
Thales's view that all of nature is based on the existence of a single ultimate substance, which he theorized to be water, was widely influential among the philosophers of his time. Thales thought the Earth floated on water.
In mathematics, Thales is the namesake of Thales's theorem, and the intercept theorem can also be referred to as Thales's theorem. Thales was said to have calculated the heights of the pyramids and the distance of ships from the shore. In science, Thales was an astronomer who reportedly predicted the weather and a solar eclipse. The discovery of the position of the constellation Ursa Major is also attributed to Thales, as well as the timings of the solstices and equinoxes. He was also an engineer, known for having allowed the Lydian army to cross the Halys River. Plutarch wrote that "at that time, Thales alone had raised philosophy from mere speculation to practice."

EVENTS (id, name, years):
Q271834  Archaic Greece (-599–-500) — period of ancient Greek history
Q175447  Babylonian captivity (-596–-537) — period in Jewish history during which a number of people from the ancient Kingdom of Judah were captives in Babylon
Q185047  Spring and Autumn period (-770–-475) — period in Chinese history from approximately 770 to 476 BCE
Q201038  Roman Kingdom (-752–-508) — period of Roman history when the city and its territory were ruled by kings (c.753–c.509 BC)
Q389688  Achaemenid Empire (-549–-329) — Iranian (Persian) empire (550–330 BC)
Q486761  classical antiquity (-799–300) — period of ancient history centered in the Mediterranean between the 8th century BCE and the 3rd century CE
Q11924845  Messenian Wars (-742–-453) — series of wars between Sparta and Messenia

work.description: the work's title if the type is wrote_in_response_to, else empty
